newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC HK bond index rose 1.15 pct to 121.38 in Nov.
newsitem.headline: HSBC HK bond index rose 1.15 pct to 121.38 in Nov.

text.p: HSBC Markets said its Hong Kong bond index rose to 121.38 in November, a 1.15 percent increase over October.
The sub-index for Hong Kong government paper increased by 1.16 percent, while the sub-index for non-Hong Kong government paper rose by 1.15 percent.

Compared with levels at end-November 1995, the overall index increased by 7.9 percent, the sub-index for Hong Kong government paper rose by 7.3 percent and the sub-index for non-Hong Kong government paper increased by 8.4 percent.
The Hong Kong bond market forged ahead in tandem with its U.S. counterpart. In addition, the steepness of the local yield curve continued to attract investors, HSBC Markets said.

With the imminent implementation of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Real Time Gross Settlement System (RTGS) on December 9, there has been strong buying interest in one- to three-month bills, resulting in spreads widening to about 90-100 basis points below local interbank rates, HSBC said.

THong Kong markets appeared to adopt the view in October that relatively weak U.S. economic data and the upcoming presidential election would convince the Federal Reserve to keep rates unchanged for the rest of 1996, HSBC said.
This, combined with the steepness of the Hong Kong dollar yield curve and ample liquidity in the market, resulted in a downward shift of the local yield curve in October, it said.
HSBC said buying interest in the longer end of the market was reflected by the strong response to the debut issue of the 10-year Exchange Fund Note on October 28, which was 13.5 times oversubscribed.
